_comment: OpenSSF Best Practices answers for the passing and silver levels, read from this file by bestpractices.dev (RepoJsonDetective) for project 13847. Every claim here is verifiable from this repository or from a command quoted in the justification. Measurements were taken on main at b661419 (v2.36.0) on 2026-07-28. Where a criterion is not met the answer says so and names the tracking issue (#68 governance, #69 roadmap, #70 assurance case, #71 test coverage, #72 doc count drift, #73 broken doc pointers, #74 shellcheck warning backlog). Gold is not answered here: bus_factor, contributors_unassociated and two_person_review all need a second maintainer.
description_good_justification: The README opens with what the software is and the problem it solves, in user-facing language: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#readme
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the whole contribution process: branching, one agent per PR, what an agent or skill definition must contain, and the pre-commit gate that runs on every commit. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements a contribution must meet: the coding standard it is held to (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/rules/coding-standards.md), the five sections every new agent definition must answer, the hook rules, and the testing expectation. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
documentation_basics_justification: The README documents what the system is, how to install it, the skills that are the entry point, and the enforcement gates: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#readme. Deeper documentation is indexed at https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#documentation, including worked session transcripts (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/EXAMPLES.md) and the memory architecture (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/MEMORY-MCP.md).
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the plugin surface a user invokes: skills, slash commands, agents, hooks and the tool CLIs. Skills and their triggers are tabulated at https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#the-entry-point-11-problem-shaped-skills; the agent file shape, frontmatter fields and routing are specified in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/AGENT-INTERNALS.md; the routing table from problem shape to agent is https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/agents/genius/INDEX.md; configuration surfaces (.zetetic.conf, .craftsmanship.conf, per-agent model and effort overrides) are documented in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md.
sites_https_justification: The project site and repository are on GitHub, HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests: searchable, each message addressable by URL, open to new participants, no proprietary client needed. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/issues
english_justification: All documentation, issues, pull requests and commit messages are in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained. Releases through v2.36.0 on 2026-07-28 and commits on main the same day: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/commits/main
repo_track_justification: Git tracks every change with author, date and message.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands on main through a pull request, so interim work is public before it is released. The eight commits between v2.34.0 and v2.35.0 are individually reviewable: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique semantic version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json and a matching git tag: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/releases
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning. Tags are of the form vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, currently v2.35.0.
version_tags_justification: Every release is an annotated git tag: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/tags
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md in Keep a Changelog format, one section per release, and the same text is published as the GitHub release body: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No vulnerability with a CVE assignment has been fixed in any release to date. Security-relevant fixes are named in the release notes when they occur: the v2.35.0 notes record all 33 CodeQL alerts cleared at source with no suppressions (issue #60) and the six Scorecard code-scanning findings closed (issue #59). https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
report_process_justification: Three issue forms (bug, feature, audit-finding) at https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/issues/new/choose, with the process described in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
report_responses_justification: Every bug report raised in the tracker has been acknowledged and closed by the maintainer, most within a day. Recent examples: #64 (redaction-checker scope), #59 (Scorecard findings), #56 (redaction backlog), #54 (advisor.md anchor), #53 (unattested session-executing artifacts). https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests use the same tracker and the same pattern. Every one raised so far was answered and resolved in a release, for example #52 (version currency) shipping in v2.35.0. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_archive_justification: Issues and pull requests are public and permanently archived: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process, what to include, and a per-severity response SLA: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private GitHub Security Advisories are enabled and SECURITY.md links the private channel directly: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received through the disclosure channel in the last six months. The commitment is documented: 24 hours first response for critical, 3 days for high, 7 days otherwise. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: Nothing is compiled. The software is Markdown agent and skill definitions plus bash and Python scripts that run directly from source; a modified file takes effect on the next session with no rebuild step. The release workflow does assemble a deterministic tarball for attestation (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/tools/build-release-bundle.sh), but that artifact is for verification rather than for making the software usable.
build_common_tools_justification: There is no build step. See the build criterion.
build_floss_tools_justification: There is no build step. See the build criterion.
test_justification: Automated suites run on every push and pull request, and the workflow shows exactly how to run each one: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml. They are the eight memory and propagation suites under scripts/, the 16 regression suites under tools/tests/*/run-tests.sh, the agent definition auditor, the craftsmanship checker, the redaction sweep and the zetetic checker. Everything is MIT-licensed with the rest of the repository.
test_invocation_justification: Each suite is invoked the standard way for its language: bash <script> for the shell suites (every one listed with its command in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) and python3 -m pytest for the Python suites, configured through the standard [tool.pytest.ini_options] table in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/pyproject.toml. The workflow is the accurate list; the commands quoted in CONTRIBUTING.md are stale and are being corrected under issue #73.
test_most_justification: Measured rather than asserted. Python statement coverage over tools/, hooks/ and scripts/ is 22 percent (2090 statements, 1628 missed, coverage.py 7.13.5 with pytest 9.0.2 on 2026-07-28, 334 tests passing); restricted to the shipped surface of hooks/ plus tools/ it is 30 percent. Three gate cores are well covered (acceptance_gate 98 percent, manifest_gate 99 percent, semantic_layer 99 percent) and the shell gates have 16 dedicated regression suites, but six Python files are at zero, including the credential denylist hook and the memory MCP server. Tracked with the full per-file measurement in issue #71.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: Every push to main and every pull request runs seven jobs, four of them hard gates that block the merge: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml, plus https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml and https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
test_policy_justification: A written policy, not an informal one. rules/coding-standards.md section 13.1 requires that every code path introduced by a change maps to a test that asserts its observable effect, and section 13.2 requires the mapping to be embedded in the pull request as a Completion Ledger. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/rules/coding-standards.md
tests_are_added_justification: Evidence from the most recent changes. v2.36.0 shipped tests/test_stop_zetetic_spine.py and tools/tests/agent-definition-auditor/run-tests.sh alongside the code they cover. v2.35.0 added tools/tests/plugin-version-check/ with 31 hermetic assertions covering every arm of the new checker, and tools/tests/release-verify/ with five tamper-rejection tests for the new bundle verifier. The fix for issue #64 shipped with the regression test that fails on the pre-fix code. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states it for hooks ("Changes to that hook need a corresponding test in tests/") and rules/coding-standards.md section 13 states it generally, with the Completion Ledger as the mechanism that makes it checkable in review. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/rules/coding-standards.md
warnings_justification: shellcheck covers the shell surface and CodeQL with the security-and-quality query pack covers the Python surface. Both run on every push, every pull request and on a weekly schedule: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml and https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: CodeQL is at zero open alerts on main: all 33 were cleared at the source with no suppressions (issue #60, recorded in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). shellcheck at error severity is at zero across hooks/ and tools/ and is a hard gate, verified by running the workflow's own command locally on 2026-07-28. The residual is 27 warning-severity shellcheck findings (most of them SC2034 unused variable), which are measured, categorised and scheduled in issue #74 rather than left unread.
warnings_strict_justification: Maximally strict for the languages in use. shellcheck runs at error severity over every shell file in hooks/ and tools/ with no "|| true" escape, so a single finding fails the job: see the step "ShellCheck (error severity - hard gate)" in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml. CodeQL runs the widest query pack, security-and-quality, rather than the default security-only pack. The redaction sweep runs under ZETETIC_PROFILE=strict, which promotes every finding to exit 1 (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml). Warning severity for shellcheck is currently informational, with the backlog measured and scheduled in issue #74.
know_secure_design_justification: The design principles are applied and written down rather than assumed. Fail-safe defaults: the memory ACL denies writes outside a scope's owner list, and tools/manifest_gate.py rejects an ungrounded source with exit 3 instead of passing it through. Least privilege: every workflow declares contents: read and the release job adds only id-token and attestations write. Open design: the whole enforcement surface is public and its limits are stated at https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#what-this-system-does-not-do
know_common_errors_justification: The vulnerability classes that matter for this software are the supply-chain ones, and they are named and countered in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md: a modified hook is code execution with the user's permissions, countered by an executable manifest, a Sigstore attestation and a verifier that checks before unpacking. Injection and traversal classes are handled by fixing what CodeQL reports at the root cause rather than annotating it away (issue #60, 33 alerts cleared, no suppressions).
crypto_published_justification: Only published and reviewed primitives are used, and none is implemented here: SHA-256 for the release checksums and executable manifest, and TLS through Python's ssl.create_default_context for outbound fetches.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptographic function is reimplemented. Hashing goes through Python hashlib and coreutils shasum, TLS through the platform's OpenSSL by way of Python's ssl module, and release signing through Sigstore.
crypto_floss_justification: OpenSSL through Python's ssl module, Python hashlib, GNU coreutils and Sigstore are all FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: SHA-256 is the only digest used anywhere in the tree, verified by grep for md5 and sha1 across tools/ and hooks/ (no hits). TLS key sizes come from Python's default context, which rejects anything below current minimums.
crypto_working_justification: No broken or known-weak algorithm is used. There is no MD5 or SHA-1 anywhere in tools/ or hooks/, and TLS is negotiated by the platform default context rather than pinned to an old suite.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The only digest in the tree is SHA-256 and the only transport is the platform default TLS context. No SHA-1, no MD5, and no hand-selected cipher mode.
crypto_pfs_justification: Outbound TLS uses ssl.create_default_context (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/tools/web_ingest.py), which negotiates ephemeral Diffie-Hellman suites by default. The software terminates no TLS of its own.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software performs no inbound authentication and stores no user passwords. It is a local plugin with no server and no accounts.
crypto_random_justification: No security-relevant random values are generated. Nothing in the tree issues tokens, nonces, salts or keys.
delivery_mitm_justification: Delivery is over HTTPS throughout: git clone and the plugin marketplace fetch from github.com over TLS, and release assets are served over HTTPS. On top of the transport, the release bundle carries a Sigstore build-provenance attestation verifiable with "gh attestation verify": https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md
delivery_unsigned_justification: Checksums are never fetched over plain HTTP. Each release publishes a .sha256 companion over HTTPS alongside a Sigstore attestation, and https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/tools/verify-release-bundle.sh checks the tarball checksum before unpacking and every executable against the manifest before running it.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no publicly known unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity. CodeQL is at zero open alerts on main and the only external dependency surface, the pinned GitHub Actions, is watched by Dependabot.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported. The two error-severity CodeQL findings that did exist (py/uninitialized-local-variable) were fixed structurally rather than annotated away, in issue #60.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed. GitHub secret scanning and push protection are both enabled on the repository (verified through the repository API on 2026-07-27), and https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/hooks/pre-tool-secret-shield.py additionally blocks any agent from reading .env, .aws/credentials, *.pem, *.key or shell history files.
static_analysis_justification: Two tools, split by language because no single tool covers both. CodeQL with the security-and-quality query pack analyses the Python hooks and tools (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml) and shellcheck analyses the shell (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml). Both run on every push to main, every pull request and on a weekly schedule, so every release is covered. The split is stated in the workflow headers rather than left as an unexplained gap.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL runs the security-and-quality suite, which is the security query pack plus the quality queries, rather than a generic lint. It found real vulnerability-class defects and they were fixed: 33 alerts cleared at source in issue #60. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Zero open CodeQL alerts on main. The full set of 33 was cleared at the source with no suppressions and no dismissals, including the two error-severity py/uninitialized-local-variable findings, which needed the functions made total rather than an annotation. Recorded in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md under v2.35.0.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every push to main, every pull request, and weekly on a schedule (CodeQL Mondays 05:00 UTC, shellcheck Wednesdays 06:00 UTC). The schedule exists because a new query pack lands out of band against code that has not changed.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No tool that varies its inputs is applied. The suites are large and hermetic but their inputs are fixed fixtures: the PII corpus is 30 hand-written fixtures scored for false positive and false negative rate, and the tools/tests suites are enumerated cases. The criterion's alternative route, an automated suite with at least 80 percent branch coverage, is not available either, since measured Python statement coverage is 22 percent (see issue #71). Property-based or fuzz input generation over the checker and parser surfaces has not been done, so this is reported unmet rather than argued into a pass.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The software is bash and Python. There is no C, C++ or other memory-unsafe code for a memory-safety dynamic analyser to target.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The suites run the software with its checks at their strictest rather than at defaults. The Python suites run under pytest with assertion rewriting active and without -O, so every assert is live. The shell suites run the gate scripts under set -euo pipefail and drive the checkers with ZETETIC_PROFILE=strict, which promotes every informational finding to a blocking exit, so a violation fails loudly during the test rather than being reported and ignored.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool of the kind this criterion describes is applied (see dynamic_analysis), so no vulnerability has been discovered by one. This becomes answerable when issue #71 lands input-varying analysis.
achieve_passing_justification: Every passing criterion is answered Met or N/A in this file.
dco_justification: There is no DCO or CLA requirement today. All non-trivial code is written by the sole maintainer, who owns the copyright and licenses it under MIT; the authorship statement is at https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#license. A DCO sign-off requirement is the intended mechanism once outside contributors start submitting non-trivial changes.
governance_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md documents the decision model. Who merges: the maintainer, the only account with write access to main. What a change needs to land: every hard CI gate green on the exact pushed tree (agent-definition auditor, craftsmanship checker on newly-added files, redaction sweep, documented-commands and documented-counts gates, tools regression suites, memory and worktree suites, shellcheck at error and warning severity, CodeQL), plus a completion ledger mapping every code path in the diff to the test or command that proves it (rules/coding-standards.md section 13). How disagreements resolve: on evidence in the open, and where evidence does not settle it the maintainer decides and records the reasoning. The document also states why there is no second-reviewer requirement (GitHub forbids self-approval, so requiring reviews on a single-maintainer repository would deadlock every merge, as already analysed in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/SCORECARD.md) and says plainly that the gates are a weaker guarantee than human review rather than presenting them as equivalent.
code_of_conduct_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, at the standard repository location, with reporting and enforcement sections. The reporting sentence points at a package.json that does not exist in this repository; that broken pointer is tracked in issue #73, and the private channel in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md works today.
roles_responsibilities_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities is a table of three roles, what each is responsible for, and who holds it. Maintainer: Clement Deust (@cdeust, admin@ai-architect.tools), who triages and closes issues, reviews and merges pull requests, cuts releases, owns the security disclosure channel and its response SLA, enforces the code of conduct, and sets the roadmap. Contributor: anyone opening an issue or pull request, holding no repository permissions. Security reporter: anyone using the private channel in SECURITY.md. The document states that the bus factor is 1 and that every role requiring a permission is held by one person, matching what docs/SCORECARD.md and the bus_factor answer here already say, rather than being softened in one place and admitted in another.
access_continuity_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity-of-access answers the criterion's three capabilities explicitly and separates what survives from what does not. Surviving with no action by anyone: the complete MIT-licensed source (no build step and no private component, so a fork is a working copy on the first clone), the full public git history and its release tags, and the verifiability of every past release, since the Sigstore build-provenance attestations are anchored in a public transparency log rather than in a signing key one person holds. Stopping, stated as such in a table: issue triage and closing, accepting changes into main, publishing a release (the workflow signs through this repository's OIDC identity), the marketplace entry, and the ai-architect.tools address used as the conduct and security reporting channel. There is no succession arrangement and none is claimed: no second person holds the keys and nothing is escrowed. The available recovery path is fork-and-continue, which the license, the public history and the transparency-log-anchored attestations make genuinely available, and the document says this is weaker than a second maintainer instead of arguing it into sufficiency. The one change that would fix it on substance is named, together with the fact that it would simultaneously unblock bus_factor, two_person_review, contributors_unassociated and the Scorecard Code-Review and Branch-Protection checks.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1. This is a single-maintainer project, stated plainly rather than papered over. The same constraint is already recorded in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/SCORECARD.md, which explains why the Scorecard Code-Review and Branch-Protection checks are structurally unreachable here: GitHub does not permit self-approval, so requiring reviews would deadlock every merge. Review rigor is carried instead by the always-on hard CI gates.
documentation_roadmap_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md covers the twelve months from 2026-07-28 to 2027-07-28 and states both halves the criterion asks for. What the project intends to do: finish OpenSSF silver and then address the four unmet-but-fixable criteria named individually (crypto_used_network, input_validation, version_tags_signed, dynamic_analysis); get Python coverage on the shipped surface to a blocking 80 percent and then move to mutation testing as the strength measure; produce a recorded end-to-end run of the autonomous build loop against a repository that does not contain this tooling; and grow the agent and skill roster under the counting gate. Each item states a Done-when condition naming the artifact that would exist or the number that would move, so a reader can check later whether it happened. What the project will not do, each as a decision with its reasoning: no sandboxing or runtime enforcement of agent refusal conditions, no hosts other than Claude Code, no hosted service or telemetry or accounts, and no localization. Gold is explicitly not promised in the window, because its three blockers all reduce to the single-maintainer fact, which depends on another person's willingness rather than on effort. Linked from the README documentation list.
documentation_architecture_justification: The architecture is documented at two levels. The component model and how the pieces compose is in the README (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#what-you-actually-get and https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#knowledge-ingestion--a-query-indexed-semantic-layer, which gives the web_ingest to manifest_gate to semantic_layer pipeline and states that the three tools import none of each other, with the skill as the single wiring point). The agent file shape, frontmatter contract and routing mechanism are specified in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/AGENT-INTERNALS.md, and the memory subsystem's scopes, ACL and MCP surface in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/MEMORY-MCP.md
documentation_security_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md states what the user can and cannot expect. It opens by naming what installing the plugin grants (session-execution rights, no sandbox between a modified file and the machine), lists the supply-chain assurances and how to verify each, and closes with an explicit "What this does NOT claim" paragraph: provenance proves who built the bundle and from which commit, not that the scripts are free of defects, and it is worth nothing to a user who never runs the verification.
documentation_quick_start_justification: Two commands and the system is installed: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#install. A narrower quick start for the gates alone (claude plugin install zetetic-gates) is on the same page, and the first thing to do with it is the reproducible one-liner at https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#the-system-enforcing-its-own-standard
documentation_current_justification: Fixed and now gated. The four disagreeing totals are reconciled against a written counting convention (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/COUNTING.md), which defines every quantity with the exact command that produces it and records the judgement calls: an agent is a file carrying a name field, so agents/genius/INDEX.md is excluded as the routing table it is; skills are counted as 11 problem-shaped entry points plus 65 category procedures totalling 76; and hooks are stated as two distinct quantities, 19 lifecycle registrations in hooks/hooks.json and 20 scripts on disk, which is what README and marketplace.json were each half-right about. Measured on 2026-07-28: 97 genius agents, 23 team agents, 120 agents total, 76 skills, 19 hook registrations, 20 hook scripts, 26 commands, 44 tools, 28 test suites. Every claim in README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and marketplace.json now agrees. Recurrence is closed by tools/doc-count-check.sh, a hard CI gate that recomputes all 25 claim instances and fails on drift; it also fails when a registered pattern matches nothing, so rewording copy cannot silently leave a claim unchecked. Unreproducible test-count claims (a tests-288 badge and a 241-tests line) were replaced by the suite count, which a command actually reports.
documentation_achievements_justification: The repository front page carries a badge row that identifies and hyperlinks the project's achievements: the live OpenSSF Best Practices badge for this project (https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/13847), live CI status, the test, agent, skill and hook counts, and the MIT license (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#readme). The badge is dynamic, so the level it displays tracks this questionnaire without a further edit. Per-release achievements are recorded in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and the security posture in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/SCORECARD.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project results have no graphical interface: they are Markdown definitions and command-line scripts whose output is plain text rendered by the host terminal. The project site is GitHub and the documentation is Markdown; the one image on the front page, the banner, carries a text alternative (alt="Zetetic Agents: 97 reasoning patterns, one epistemic standard").
internationalization_justification: The tools' user-facing strings (checker findings, hook notices, setup output) are English literals and are not externalized for localization, and the agent and skill definitions are English prose. Externalizing them has not been done, so this is reported unmet rather than claimed.
sites_password_security_justification: The project operates no site of its own that authenticates external users. The repository and the download URLs are GitHub, and no password is stored by this project.
maintenance_or_update_justification: There is a documented upgrade path and the project keeps it working. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md gives a five-step adoption path for an existing non-compliant project, from permissive through standard to strict. Version currency is enforced rather than assumed: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/tools/plugin-version-check.sh compares installed, pinned and released versions and names which of the two possible lags applies and who fixes it, and it runs at session start. Upgrade-relevant changes are called out per release in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. The commitment is documented: reporters are credited in the release notes for the patched version unless they request anonymity. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md documents the whole response process: the private advisory channel, what a report must contain, a per-severity SLA table (24 hours first response and 7 days to patch for critical, 3 and 14 days for high), a five-step disclosure timeline with a 30-day default coordinated date, and what is out of scope.
coding_standards_justification: The standard is a document in the tree, not a preference: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/rules/coding-standards.md covers SOLID, the layer dependency rule, size limits, dependency injection, local reasoning, source discipline, mutation testing, the definition of done and the boy-scout rule, each with its primary source. CONTRIBUTING.md names it as binding and excerpts the load-bearing rules: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Enforced automatically at two points. At commit time https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/hooks/pre-commit-zetetic.sh runs tools/zetetic-checker.sh on the staged diff and returns exit 2 on a violation. In CI four hard gates block the merge (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml): the craftsmanship checker on newly added files, the redaction sweep on the full tree under ZETETIC_PROFILE=strict, the tools regression suite, and shellcheck at error severity. The ratchet shape (new files gated, legacy debt reported) is documented in the workflow itself.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries are generated. There is no compiler or linker invocation anywhere in the project, so CC, CFLAGS and LDFLAGS have nothing to apply to.
build_preserve_debug_justification: There is no build or installation system that strips anything. The software is Markdown and scripts, installed by copying, and the source on disk is what runs.
build_non_recursive_justification: There is no build system, so there are no subdirectory builds to make recursive or otherwise.
build_repeatable_justification: Although nothing is compiled, the one thing that is generated is bit-for-bit reproducible by construction. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/tools/build-release-bundle.sh creates the release tarball with --sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner, so the archive does not depend on filesystem order, timestamps or the building user. The script says why: an attestation over a non-deterministic archive proves nothing a second builder can check.
installation_common_justification: Installed and uninstalled through the ecosystem's package manager: "claude plugin marketplace add cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents" then "claude plugin install zetetic-team-subagents" (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#install). The manual path is https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/scripts/setup.sh with install, update, uninstall and configure verbs, and the installer writes a manifest so that uninstall removes exactly what it added.
installation_standard_variables_justific: There is no installation system that writes built artifacts to a configurable prefix. Installation copies agents, skills, hooks and tools into the host's own plugin directory under ~/.claude, which is the convention the host defines, so DESTDIR and similar variables have nothing to select.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone and the software is complete: nothing is compiled and there are no dependencies to resolve. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md lists the prerequisites (bash 4+, GNU coreutils, ripgrep, python3) and https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml gives the exact command for every suite, which is the same command a developer runs locally. The stale command list inside CONTRIBUTING is being corrected under issue #73.
external_dependencies_justification: Listed in two computer-processable forms. Every release publishes a CycloneDX SBOM (zetetic-team-subagents.cdx.json) inventorying every bundled file with its hash, including the vendored third-party skill material, alongside an EXECUTABLE-MANIFEST.sha256 that enumerates every hook and tool that will run on the user's machine (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md). The only external supply-chain surface, the GitHub Actions, is declared in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml and each action is pinned to a full commit SHA in the workflows.
dependency_monitoring_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml runs weekly against the github-actions ecosystem, which is this project's only external dependency surface: there is no runtime package to install, so there is no pip or npm manifest to watch, and the config states that reasoning rather than declaring an empty ecosystem. Dependabot updates the pinned SHA and rewrites the version comment in place, so pinning discipline is preserved automatically. OpenSSF Scorecard runs on a schedule on top of it (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/scorecard.yml), with each finding's disposition recorded in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/docs/SCORECARD.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are identifiable and updateable. The GitHub Actions are pinned by full commit SHA with a version comment and updated by Dependabot weekly. The Python code imports only the standard library, so there is no vendored runtime dependency to go stale. The one convenience copy, the vendored writing and redaction rule material, carries its provenance in the file and is inventoried in the per-release CycloneDX SBOM.
interfaces_current_justification: The technology stack is current and nothing deprecated is relied on. The Python is standard library only (argparse, hashlib, json, ssl, subprocess, urllib, xml.etree, tempfile) with no deprecated or removed module, and CI pins Python 3.12. The shell targets bash 4+ with POSIX coreutils, and shellcheck at error severity would flag obsolete constructs on every push.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Every push to main and every pull request runs the full gate set and reports pass or fail per job: seven jobs in https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml (memory suites, agent auditor, worktree tests, zetetic checker, craftsmanship checker, redaction sweep, tools regression suite covering 16 suites), plus shellcheck and CodeQL in their own workflows. Four of them are hard gates that block the merge. The Python pytest suites are the one part not yet wired into CI, tracked in issue #71.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Well above 50 percent, because the standard makes it mandatory: rules/coding-standards.md section 13.1 G2 requires every bug fixed in a pull request to carry a regression test that fails on the pre-fix code. Recent fixes follow it: issue #64 (redaction-checker missing untracked files) shipped with the test that reproduces the false local pass, and issue #60's CodeQL fix was made structural so the checker itself is the regression guard. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/rules/coding-standards.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Measured, not estimated. coverage.py 7.13.5 with pytest 9.0.2 on 2026-07-28 over tools/, hooks/ and scripts/: 2090 statements, 1628 missed, 22 percent, with 334 tests passing. Restricting the source set to the shipped surface of hooks/ plus tools/ and dropping the one-shot scripts/patch_*.py migrations gives 30 percent, so the answer does not change under a friendlier scoping. Three gate cores are near-complete (acceptance_gate 98 percent, manifest_gate 99 percent, semantic_layer 99 percent) while six files are at zero, including hooks/pre-tool-secret-shield.py and tools/memory-mcp-server.py. N/A is not available here: coverage.py is a FLOSS tool that measures Python, which is one of this project's languages. The full per-file measurement and the acceptance criteria are in issue #71.
test_policy_mandated_justification: A formal written policy exists. rules/coding-standards.md section 13.1 A1 to A3 requires happy paths, every enumerated edge case and every failure path (including the emission of the signal itself) to map to a test, and section 13.2 makes the mapping a required artifact of the pull request. Section 13.3 enumerates the refusals, including that classifying a coverage gap in new code as a follow-up is blocking. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/rules/coding-standards.md
implement_secure_design_justification: The principles are implemented, with one stated exception. Fail-safe defaults: the memory ACL denies any write outside a scope's owner list and tools/manifest_gate.py rejects an ungrounded source with exit 3. Separation of privilege: the release job holds only id-token and attestations write, everything else is contents: read. Open design: the enforcement surface and its documented limits are public (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents#what-this-system-does-not-do). Economy of mechanism: web_ingest, manifest_gate and semantic_layer import none of each other and are wired by a skill, so each is independently testable. The exception is complete mediation at one tool boundary, described under input_validation below.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The project selects no cryptographic algorithm of its own. Transport algorithms are negotiated by the platform TLS stack and release signing is delegated to Sigstore, so there is no project-level choice for a user to switch.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software processes no authentication credentials and holds no private keys. Release signing is keyless through Sigstore, where the signing certificate is short-lived and issued against the workflow's OIDC identity, so there is no stored private key to separate out or rotate.
crypto_used_network_justification: Outbound fetches use the platform TLS stack correctly, but insecure schemes are not disabled by default. tools/web_ingest.py hands a caller-supplied URL to the standard library client without restricting the scheme first, so plain HTTP is accepted on the same footing as HTTPS. The fix is an allowlist at that boundary, re-applied after each redirect hop, with plain HTTP available only behind an explicit opt-in. Reported unmet rather than argued around.
crypto_tls12_justification: Outbound TLS goes through ssl.create_default_context (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/tools/web_ingest.py), whose minimum protocol version on the Python versions this project targets is TLS 1.2. The context is created once and reused for every fetch, including the robots.txt fetch, so no request escapes it.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Certificate verification is on by default and is never disabled. ssl.create_default_context sets verify_mode to CERT_REQUIRED and check_hostname to True, and there is no CERT_NONE, no check_hostname = False and no unverified context anywhere in the tree. The context is preferentially built against certifi's CA bundle when available, falling back to the system store. https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/tools/web_ingest.py
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: No private information is ever sent. The outbound client transmits only a User-Agent, Accept-Encoding and the conditional-GET validators (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since); it sends no cookie, no authorization header and no credential. Certificate verification is performed by the default context before any request body or header leaves, and no fetch is made outside that context.
signed_releases_justification: Every release is cryptographically signed through Sigstore and the verification path is documented. The release workflow attests the tarball, the executable manifest and the CycloneDX SBOM with actions/attest-build-provenance under a least-privilege OIDC identity, and self-verifies with the shipped verifier before publishing (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml). Users verify with "gh attestation verify zetetic-team-subagents.tar.gz --repo cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents", documented at https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md. Signing is keyless, so no private key exists to be stored on the distribution site: the certificate is short-lived, issued by Fulcio against the workflow's identity, and logged in the Rekor transparency log.
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated but not cryptographically signed: "git tag -v v2.35.0" reports no signature. The release artifacts are covered instead, each with a SHA-256 companion and a Sigstore build-provenance attestation (https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md). Signing the tags themselves would add a second, independent anchor and has not been set up.
input_validation_justification: Validation at the trust boundaries is mostly present and in one place it is the wrong shape. The memory tool checks every scope write against an owner list, tools/manifest_gate.py rejects an ungrounded source with a non-zero exit rather than passing it through, the hooks bound their stdin reads, and the fetch path caps response size and redirect depth. The gap is that one tool accepts a caller-supplied URL and validates the scheme with a downstream denylist rather than an allowlist at the boundary, which this criterion asks for explicitly. The maintainer has the specifics; the fix is to allowlist the accepted schemes where the input enters and re-check after each redirect hop, with a regression test for the rejected cases.
hardening_justification: This criterion counts mechanisms such as HTTP response headers and compiler hardening flags, and explicitly excludes least privilege. The project produces no HTTP surface for a Content Security Policy to apply to and compiles nothing, so there is no -fstack-protector equivalent to enable. The protections it does use (bounded stdin reads, a response-size cap, a redirect cap, fail-closed gates and a credential-path denylist on agent reads) are real, but they are not what this criterion measures, so it is reported unmet rather than argued into a pass.
assurance_case_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/zetetic-team-subagents/blob/main/SECURITY.md covers two of the four required parts: it describes the threat (everything shipped executes in the user's session with no sandbox, and the payload does not even need to be compiled) and it argues that common implementation weaknesses are countered (shellcheck, CodeQL, Scorecard, the attested bundle and the install-path verifier). It does not identify trust boundaries as such and it makes no secure-design argument, so the assurance case is incomplete. Tracked with the four required parts as acceptance criteria in issue #70.
